# Description

<!-- page X -->

## Description

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=50%}

![](images/image_DataMetadata.png){width=80%}

> A data paper is a scientific **publication that precisely describes a data set**, and informs the scientific community of its existence, its methods and its potential for reuse[^8]

:::

::: {.column .center width=50%}

![[Garnier _et al._ (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1002/ecy.70219)](images/image-data-paper-garnier.png){width=70%}

:::

::::

[^8]: [IRD](https://data.ird.fr/datapapers/)

<!-- page 8 -->

## Sections

A scientific publication whose primary purpose is to describe a data set or group of data sets, rather than to report a research investigation.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=50%}
<br>

- **DOI**: for indexing and citation. Data Papers are indexed by Web of Science, 
PubMedCentral, Scopus, Google Scholar, Directory of Open Access Journal (DOAJ), etc..
<br>
<br>
- **Title**: promotion and publicizing data
<br>
<br>
- **Authors**: acknowledgement and credit for data publishers through scientific publication
<br>
<br>
- **Abstract**: description of data in a structured, human-readable form
<br>
<br>
- **Other sections** : material and methods, taxonomic coverage, geographic coverage, descriptive statistics, etc.

:::

::: {.column width=50%}

![](images/image-data-paper-bioblitz.jpg){width=70% fig-align="right"}

:::

::::

## Integrated Publishing Toolkit - IPT


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=50%}

<br>
The [IPT](https://www.gbif.org/fr/ipt), developed by the GBIF:
<br>

- is a **free open-source software**

- is used by organizations around the world to create and manage repositories for sharing biodiversity datasets

- facilitates the **filling of metadata** and the automated production of a Data Paper

:::

![](images/image-data-paper-ipt.png){width=80% fig-align='right'}

:::

# Process

## A good level of FAIRness

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width=50%}

- Open data (CC-BY 4.0 compatible with Etalab)
- Mandatory license
- Direct link to download raw datasets
- Thematic scope (All biodiversity including paleo- and archaeo-biodiversity)
- Geographic scope (Data produced by France)
- Temporal coverage (at least one data acquisition date)
- Abstract
- Title, authors and contacts
- Acquisition framework (at least via a text field)
- DOI / unique identifiers
- taxonomic coverage (if taxa are present)
- keywords related to the Thesaurus
- Data attributes (Dictionary of data attributes with units and descriptions)
- Semantic annotation (Keywords and attribute names, unlimited usable resources)
:::
